backlog.spec: Set MATRIX_LR = 0.03.

backlog.title: Weight decay linearly decayed

backlog.spec: Set EMBEDDING_LR = 0.4 to test whether 0.6 is too high.
backlog.title: Embedding LR 0.4

backlog.spec: Set UNEMBEDDING_LR = 0.008, doubling the lm_head LR.

backlog.spec: Set SCALAR_LR = 0.25 to reduce the step size on the per-layer scalars.
backlog.title: Scalar LR 0.25

backlog.spec: Change ADAM_BETAS to (0.9, 0.99) for stability, or at least beta1 0.9. Test the effect.
backlog.title: Adam beta2 0.99 for embeddings

backlog.spec: Change the Muon momentum schedule so that it ramps from 0.85 to 0.97 over the first 200 steps (then holds), instead of the current ramp. If the ramp is shorter, extend it.
backlog.title: Muon momentum warmup tuning

backlog.spec: Reduce the logit softcap value from its current value (likely 30) to 15. If there is no softcap, add 15*tanh(x/15) to the logits before the loss.
backlog.title: Logit softcap 15

backlog.spec: Replace the MLP activation with SwiGLU, using hidden size 8/3*dim rounded to a multiple of 64, so the parameter count stays the same. Use three matrices, all Muon-optimized.
backlog.title: ReLU^2 MLP to SwiGLU

backlog.spec: If value embeddings are on alternating layers, add them to every layer or remove them from half of the layers. Measure which is better at equal time.
backlog.title: Untied value embeddings on fewer layers

backlog.spec: Initialize the attention output projection and the MLP output projection to zero if they are not already, so that the residual stream starts as identity.
backlog.title: Zero-init projection tweaks

backlog.spec: After the QK RMS norm, multiply q and k by a factor of 1.2 each, which sharpens attention. Alternatively use a learnable per-head scalar initialized at 1.2.
backlog.title: QK norm scale

backlog.spec: Make sure the optimizer step uses fused AdamW and that the loss uses a chunked cross-entropy. Do not change the numerics. The goal is higher throughput and more tokens in 300 s.
backlog.title: Remove unused compile overhead: torch.compile max-autotune off, fused ops

backlog.spec: Add torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0) before the optimizer step to damp spikes at the high LRs.

backlog.spec: Increase the RoPE base frequency from 10000 to 50000. This may help or hurt at short sequence lengths, so test it cheaply.
backlog.title: RoPE base 50000

backlog.spec: Change the initial per-layer residual scale (resid_lambdas) from 1.0 to 0.9 and the x0 skip lambdas from 0.1 to 0.2, if these scalars exist. Otherwise add them as learnable scalars.
backlog.title: Residual lambda init tweak

backlog.spec: In the attention module, after the QK RMS norm, multiply both q and k by 1.3 (instead of 1.2 from slot 0), making attention logits about 1.69x sharper. This probes whether the slot 0 gain (-0.0021) is real and whether the optimum is higher. Change nothing else.
backlog.title: Replicate q/k scale 1.2 with 1.3

backlog.spec: After QK norm, replace the fixed q/k scaling with a learnable per-head scalar parameter (shape n_head, init 1.2**2 applied to q only, i.e. q = q * s[None,None,:,None]). Put the parameter in the scalar Adam group using SCALAR_LR, with no weight decay. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Learnable per-head attention scale

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**17 with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64 (accumulation of 1 or fewer, adjust code if needed) and scale all LRs (matrix, embedding, unembedding, scalar) by 0.7 to compensate for the noisier gradients. This tests a much more step-heavy regime.
backlog.title: Batch 2**17 with 0.7x LRs

backlog.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO = 0.03 and FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.05. Combine these two schedule tweaks into one run, to check that a tiny warmup stabilises early Muon steps and that a small LR floor helps the end of the run.
backlog.title: Short linear warmup 3% plus nonzero final LR 0.05

backlog.spec: Change the logit softcap constant in the forward pass (the value in softcap * tanh(logits/softcap)) from its current value to 15. Nothing else changes. It tests whether tighter capping regularises the output distribution in this short training regime.
backlog.title: Logit softcap 15 with SwiGLU-free tweak

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH = 6 and ASPECT_RATIO = 96 (model_dim 576; make sure it is a multiple of HEAD_DIM 128, otherwise use 640 via ASPECT_RATIO 107 or round up). A shallower, wider model is faster per step and sees more tokens in 300 s. Keep other settings.
backlog.title: Depth 6 with ASPECT_RATIO 96

backlog.spec: Before the optimizer step, call torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0) after the accumulated backward passes. Keep everything else the same. It guards against loss spikes at high LR.
backlog.title: Gradient clipping at 1.0

backlog.spec: Change the Muon momentum schedule so the final momentum is 0.97 instead of the current plateau (typically 0.95), reaching it at the same point in the ramp. Smoother updates may help late in the run. Do not change anything else.
backlog.title: Muon momentum 0.97 plateau

backlog.spec: Set WINDOW_PATTERN = "SSSS" so the code's rule that forces the final layer to be full-context still applies (or add that rule if absent). Shorter windows make attention cheaper and give more steps in the time budget. Compare against SSSL.
backlog.title: Window pattern all-short except last layer

backlog.spec: Set WARMUP_RATIO = 0.03 and FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.05. Change nothing else. This gives a gentle start for Muon and Adam and avoids a hard zero LR at the end of the time-based schedule.
backlog.title: Short warmup plus nonzero final LR

backlog.spec: Where the logits are computed, apply logits = 15 * tanh(logits / 15) before the cross-entropy loss. If a softcap already exists, change its value to 15. Do this in float32 for the softcap op. Do not touch the evaluation path. If the softcap sits inside the model forward that evaluation uses, that is fine as long as the forward signature is unchanged.
backlog.title: Logit softcap 15

backlog.spec: Before optimizer.step() in the training loop, call torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0) after the last micro-step backward. This stabilizes early training with high Adam LRs, such as the embedding LR of 0.6. Make sure the clip runs once per optimizer step and not per micro-batch.
backlog.title: Gradient clipping at 1.0

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH = 10 and ASPECT_RATIO = 52 so model_dim is 520, rounded to a multiple of HEAD_DIM 128 as the existing code does (this gives 512 or 640, so check the rounding). Aim for a comparable parameter count with more depth. If the rounding gives dim 640, use ASPECT_RATIO = 51 to land on 512 instead. Keep the other hyperparameters unchanged. This tests whether depth over width helps at the 300 s budget.
backlog.title: Depth 10 with narrower aspect ratio

backlog.spec: Set HEAD_DIM = 64 so the model has twice as many attention heads at the same width. Make sure the number of KV heads follows the head count, and that the rotary embedding and value-embedding code use the new head count. Change nothing else.
backlog.title: HEAD_DIM 64

backlog.spec: Find the Muon momentum schedule, which usually ramps from 0.85 to 0.95 over the first 300 steps. Change it to ramp from 0.85 to 0.97 over the first 200 steps, then hold at 0.97. If the warmdown phase also changes momentum, keep that behavior. Change nothing else.
backlog.title: Muon momentum 0.97 plateau with shorter ramp

backlog.spec: Make Muon's cautious weight decay follow the training progress. Use wd = 0.2 * (1 - progress), where progress is elapsed time / budget, updated each step in the same place the LR and momentum schedules are updated. This keeps the strong early regularization and removes it near the end, when the LR is also small.
backlog.title: Linearly decaying weight decay

backlog.spec: Change the rotary embedding base from 10000 to 50000, then set EMBEDDING_LR = 0.4. This is one change to position encoding and token-embedding stability. The two edits are small and interact only weakly.
backlog.title: RoPE base 50000 with lower embedding LR

backlog.spec: Initialize lm_head weights to zero if they are not already, and set UNEMBEDDING_LR = 0.008. Zero logits at init give a clean uniform starting loss, and the larger LR lets the output head move faster in a short run. If lm_head is already zero-initialised, only change the LR.
backlog.title: Zero-init the lm_head and raise its LR

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18 (keep DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64, so grad accumulation halves). In a fixed 300 s budget a smaller batch gives about twice as many optimizer steps, which usually helps a short run. Keep all LRs unchanged. If the code asserts divisibility, make sure 2**18 is divisible by DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE*MAX_SEQ_LEN.
backlog.title: Batch 2**18 tokens per step

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**17 and multiply MATRIX_LR, EMBEDDING_LR, UNEMBEDDING_LR and SCALAR_LR by 0.7 (e.g. MATRIX_LR 0.028, EMBEDDING_LR 0.42, UNEMBEDDING_LR 0.0028, SCALAR_LR 0.35). Four times as many steps at a smaller batch size; the LR scaling roughly follows the sqrt rule. Muon momentum schedule left unchanged.
backlog.title: Batch 2**17 with LRs scaled by 0.7

backlog.spec: After the QK RMS norm in attention, multiply both q and k by 1.3 (attention logits scale 1.69x). This tests the one signal that helped in slot 0 (1.2) at a nearby, stronger value. It is a fixed constant with no learnable parameter.
backlog.title: Q/K scale 1.2 replicate with 1.3

backlog.spec: Set HEAD_DIM = 64 so that dim 512 gives 8 heads instead of 4. More heads with smaller dims often gives better quality at this scale. Make no other change; check that rotary embeddings and value-embedding shapes follow n_head and head_dim.
backlog.title: HEAD_DIM 64

backlog.spec: Set FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.1 so the warmdown ends at 10% of the peak LR rather than 0. Because training is stopped by the wall-clock, a non-zero floor may avoid wasting the last few steps at a vanishing LR.
backlog.title: Final LR fraction 0.1

backlog.spec: Change the rotary embedding base frequency from 10000 to 50000 in the precomputed cos/sin tables. This is a one-constant change that alters the positional frequency spectrum and may help the long-window layers.
backlog.title: RoPE base 50000

backlog.spec: Initialise lm_head weights to zero (instead of small normal) and raise UNEMBEDDING_LR from 0.004 to 0.008. Zero logits at the start give a uniform prediction and cleaner early gradients to the trunk, and the larger LR compensates. Make no other change.
backlog.title: Zero-init lm_head with a higher LR
